findings.issue: The claimed detection bound is false in the live system. The watchdog skips both cadence stalls and standby-backlog alerts when the Claude PID is absent, while the in-session fallback dies with that process. A quiet process-dead seat can therefore remain invisible indefinitely. Even with a live PID, fallback values of 1800–3600s imply roughly 90–180 minutes before threshold, plus the watchdog sweep interval.
findings.suggestion: Detect stale seat-authored heartbeats regardless of PID. Add an absolute external canary that event wakes cannot reset, use fenced revival, publish the numeric detection SLO, and test the process-dead/no-mail case.

findings.issue: “Drain, then baseline with no replay” creates a lost-wake window: mail appended after drain enumeration but before watcher baseline becomes history and does not ring. Moreover, msg.sh advances its byte cursor when mail is printed, before its side effect is recorded; a crash after read logically loses the message. Concurrent wakes can also double-read or regress the unlocked cursor.
findings.suggestion: Preserve the governing spec’s two-cursor design: the watcher cursor is observational, while the processing cursor commits only after an idempotent side effect keyed by hub_id. Arm by comparing stream head with the processing cursor. Use monotonic locked cursor commits and crash/race fixtures.

findings.issue: Four independent wake sources exist without single-flight or fencing. Doorbell, fallback, task completion, and revival can coincide; restarts may also create duplicate monitors. On Codex, concurrent external pokes could become concurrent turns. Drain-whole does not prevent duplicate irreversible actions.
findings.suggestion: Require every external invocation to acquire the per-seat revival lease already defined by SEAT_PROTOCOL. Add a per-seat pending bit and watcher generation so signals coalesce into one turn and restarted watchers supersede earlier generations.

findings.issue: A 60-second poll does not guarantee seat-level coalescing: the draft emits one event per grown sender file, so six replies may cause six notifications. Sol completion creates two signals for the invoking seat—task exit and completion mail. Relying on harness rate-limit kills as a backstop converts overload into liveness loss and restart thrash.
findings.suggestion: Use edge-triggered per-seat coalescing: wake only on pending false→true, suppress further pokes until the processing cursor catches the head, impose a quiet window/minimum inter-wake interval, and deduplicate Sol signals by run_id. Add global concurrency limits and prohibit acknowledgements for informational mail.

findings.issue: The draft conflates durable completion recording, coordination latency, and fleet pacing. Completion mail fixes durability without requiring fleet-wide per-append wakes. A 1800-second fallback saves nothing for existing 1800-second seats, increases empty wakes for 2700-second seats, and becomes more expensive than periodic batching once event groups exceed roughly 1–2 per hour. No token-cost evidence supports the premise.
findings.suggestion: Separate durable transport from interrupt policy. Measure cached and uncached input tokens, output/tool tokens, and cost per useful message. Give coordination seats low-latency total-inbound wakes; let doing seats wake immediately only for alert/request/dispatch and batch routine info/status traffic.

findings.issue: Model-authored “verify watcher alive” is a paper invariant. The cadence context is unstructured, overwritten each wake, and can repeat stale belief. One successful event proves no future liveness. Restart may kill the monitor, while resume may leave an old monitor and create duplicates. Compaction is not solved by asking the compacted model to inspect its task list.
findings.suggestion: Move ownership to a host supervisor or central broker. Store watcher generation, target session handle, last_poll_at, last_poke_at, and pending head in the authoritative seat registry. Have launch/revival manage it mechanically and verify it using synthetic end-to-end canaries.

findings.issue: The normative glob from-*-to-<letter> excludes from-*-to-all broadcasts, although msg.sh read consumes both and §6 discusses broadcast storms. Interpreted literally, broadcasts will not ring seats. A watcher that resolves its glob only once also misses mailbox files created later by new senders.
findings.suggestion: Define inbound as direct-to-letter plus to-all, with dynamic discovery, canonical lowercase names, and intentional self-origin exclusions. Prefer a mailbox-head API so watcher and watchdog do not independently reproduce fragile filename semantics.

findings.issue: “Host-side watcher … or a protocol-defined drain point” is not a mechanism-neutral contract: a drain point is not wake-on-append. No Codex invocation, modal, lease, timeout, acknowledgement, or failure semantics are defined. The draft claims a fleet primitive while a planned runtime has no conforming implementation.
findings.suggestion: Either scope ratification to Claude seats or require a capability adapter per runtime. For Codex, specify and test exec-resume/tmux invocation, modal handling, lease acquisition, timeout, acknowledgement, and cadence/report-only fallback when external_invoke is unavailable.

findings.issue: The draft never declares whether doorbell seats are active/sleeping or standby. The choice changes the live watchdog predicate: standby checks backlog but the helper forces cadence_seconds=0; sleeping supports fallback cadence but does not check undrained backlog. The current host watchdog also lacks the governing spec’s quiet heartbeat-floor predicate. Therefore “watchdog unchanged” is incompatible with the design.
findings.suggestion: Define one canonical state machine and migrate cadence helper, ingester, watchdog, launcher, and registry together. Standby must have both oldest-undrained-mail and independent quiet-heartbeat-floor predicates.

findings.issue: Two light Claude seats for three days or 20 events avoids the risky cases and is statistically weak. With zero misses in 20 events, the approximate 95% upper bound remains 15%; a true 1% miss has only about an 18% chance of appearing. Median latency hides tails, and fallback-rescued doorbell failures may be miscounted as successes. The Sol path ships after the pilot, so the claimed unified behavior is not tested.
findings.suggestion: Begin with deterministic conformance and shadow-mode replay, then soak diverse roles including a high-fan-in coordinator and Codex adapter. Inject arm races, watcher/process death, compaction, duplicate restart, broadcast/reply bursts, dual Sol signals, and simultaneous fallback. Track p50/p95/max event-to-turn and event-to-cursor-commit, fallback rescues, duplicates, lease conflicts, backlog age, watcher uptime, and token cost. Require hundreds of events for a low miss-rate claim.

findings.issue: The current JV SEAT_PROTOCOL already contains stronger doorbell guarantees: separate cursors, missed-event-safe comparison, quiet-window coalescing, leased wakes, oldest-undrained detection, a canary floor, capability negotiation, and own-mailbox versus total-inbound policies. This draft omits or contradicts those invariants while proposing another wake section, creating a regression or competing source of truth.
findings.suggestion: Rebase the amendment on the actual current SEAT_PROTOCOL. Express only genuine deltas, retain its existing invariants, and remove conflicting prose rather than introducing a second contract.

findings.issue: Resetting the fallback timer on every wake means it cannot audit watcher health while other task notifications remain frequent. Watcher restart also has no backoff or circuit breaker.
findings.suggestion: Use an absolute external canary schedule that unrelated activity cannot postpone, and supervise watcher restart with bounded backoff plus an explicit degraded-state alert.

strongest_aspect: The draft correctly distinguishes durable mailbox evidence from ephemeral harness notifications. Mailing Sol completion is a sound and independently valuable change, and drain-whole is the right interpretation of a doorbell edge.
biggest_risk: The protocol can certify a dead or deaf seat as acceptably quiet: watcher and fallback share the session failure domain, the live watchdog ignores absent processes, and the baseline/cursor scheme can lose the edge intended to restore liveness.
